title: Partner marketplace onboarding scenarios and copy templates
summary: Working draft: scenario-driven checklist and copy templates to accelerate partner listings across AWS Marketplace, Azure Marketplace, and GCP Marketplace. Focus: reduce back-and-forth by surfacing common acceptance gate answers, persona-specific copy, and acceptance test scenarios.
body:
Purpose and scope

This is a practical, scenario-first playbook for partner onboarding to cloud marketplaces. Goal is to provide: (1) a short checklist for technical/legal/product gates that usually block listings, (2) ready-to-use copy snippets for different buyer personas and cloud marketplaces, and (3) acceptance/test scenarios for the partner/engineering teams to run before submission. Keep this doc lightweight and used as the operational template to attach to partner intake tickets.

How to use this doc
- GTM or partner manager attaches this doc to the initial intake.
- Engineering or partner success runs the acceptance scenarios and fills the checklist.
- Copy snippets are chosen per target audience (startup, mid-market, enterprise) and edited for SKU/pricing details.
- Resolve legal/security items before final submission (see gating section).

Acceptance gates (common blockers) — quick checklist
- Product metadata: Product name matches legal entity and trademark checks (pass/fail)
- SKU and billing: SKU mapping defined + sample pricing tiers attached
- Deployment model: Hosted API / Dedicated / Private – validated and clearly documented
- OAuth/IAM integration docs: sample roles, least-privilege policies included
- Network architecture diagram: VPC flow, egress rules, and where data is stored (region)
- Compliance artifacts: SOC2 summary, data processing addendum, encryption at rest and transit notes
- Support plan: on-call contact, severity matrix, SLAs for Dedicated/Private customers
- Security review: pen test summary or date for planned pen test; known CVEs list
- Billing/legal: sample MSA excerpt or link to portal license, refund/cancellation terms

Notes on priority: items marked with * are frequently cause for rejection during marketplace QA.

Persona-specific listing copy templates (short variants for marketplace listing)
- Startup / Developer-first (50–120 chars):
  "Redwood Inference — low-latency LLM inference platform | simple API, predictable pricing, and dev-friendly SDKs for building real-time generative features."

- Mid-market / Product teams (50–140 chars):
  "Production-grade LLM inference with observability, reserved capacity, and enterprise controls — reduce inference cost and ensure predictable latency at scale."

- Enterprise / Platform teams (70–160 chars):
  "Unified inference runtime for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. SLA-backed capacity, VPC/on‑prem options, and audit-ready controls for regulated workloads."

Long-form description (400–600 chars) — marketplace body copy, neutral tone
"Redwood Inference provides a high-performance platform for serving large language models across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Ship LLM features using a single API with built-in routing, caching, and cost controls. Use dedicated GPU pools for predictable throughput or deploy a private control plane for regulated data. Includes tracing, model rollouts, and monitoring to keep production models reliable and cost-effective."

Feature bullets (short list)
- Simple REST + SDKs: text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking
- Deployment modes: hosted API, reserved capacity, private VPC/on‑prem
- Observability: per-route latency, token cost breakdowns, and tracing
- Reliability: canary rollouts, fallback policies, and SLA options
- Cost controls: batching, KV caching, and quantization recommendations

Cloud-specific callouts (brief)
- AWS Marketplace: highlight AMI/container if offering private appliance or BYOL licensing. Ensure product code and usage SKUs are aligned. Provide CloudFormation snippets for automation.
- Azure: include managed offer manifest notes and ARM template examples for Private Offer configurations.
- GCP: listing should include marketplace VM/container images and clear region support and network egress expectations.

Acceptance/test scenarios (runbook for partner/eng)
- Scenario A — Basic listing smoke test (5–10 min)
  Steps: confirm product metadata, upload logo, verify short description, and submit for preview. Expected: no validation errors for mandatory fields.

- Scenario B — Billing SKU smoke (15–30 min)
  Steps: map internal pricing tiers to marketplace SKUs, simulate usage billing for a small account, check invoice format and SKU tagging in reports. Expected: correct mapping and reportable metrics.

- Scenario C — Private deployment preflight (1–2 days)
  Steps: provide VPC architecture diagram, sample deployment script (Terraform/ARM/CloudFormation), KMS/HSM integration notes, and acceptance tests for network isolation. Expected: architecture doc reviewed by cloud partner and security sign-off.

- Scenario D — Security/compliance checklist (variable)
  Steps: attach SOC2 summary, describe data retention and deletion controls, provide encryption and key management details, and note upcoming pen test schedule. Expected: compliance artifacts attached and any gaps tracked as JIRA items.

Copy variants for solution pages and tile images
- Tile headline options (short):
  - "Predictable LLM inference — fast, cost-aware"
  - "Serve large models with SLA-backed capacity"
  - "Bring your model to production — hosted, reserved, or private"

- 1-line benefit overlays for tile images:
  - "Reduce per-token cost with smart batching"
  - "SLA-backed latency targets for mission-critical features"

Submission tips and common fixes from past listings
- Avoid overly productized marketing claims about model capabilities (e.g., "best-in-class accuracy") — marketplaces flag unsubstantiated claims.
- Include at least one screenshot of the console showing model rollout or observability dashboards.
- For private/VPC offers, attach a downloadable deployment guide (PDF) with command snippets.
- Prepare short template responses for marketplace QA questions (fast turnaround reduces rejection cycles).

Open questions / items to resolve before finalizing listing
- Which SKU mapping will finance prefer for reserved capacity (monthly commit vs. consumption)? (Action: Priya to confirm by Oct 20)
- Do we include a free trial credit coupon for first-time users on each marketplace? Pros/cons: AWS allows promotional codes in some programs — need legal sign-off.
- Do we submit separate offers for Dedicated and Private, or use one offer with feature toggles? (Engineering and Sales input required)

To-do (next steps)
- [ ] Attach final SOC2 snapshot and verified pen test date (Tom)
- [ ] Finalize SKU names and pricing table (Finance)
- [ ] Generate CloudFormation and ARM example templates (Infra eng)
- [ ] Create high-res tile image and two alternate headlines (Design)

Appendix — quick FAQ snippets for marketplace QA
Q: Where is customer data stored?
A: Regional controls — customers may choose region for hosted deployments; private/dedicated stays in tenant-managed VPC or provisioned region. See deployment guide for region mapping.

Q: How do you handle keys?
A: Customers may use Redwood-managed KMS or bring-your-own (BYOK) via partner KMS/HSM integrations for Private offers.

Contact/owner notes
- Primary owner: Asha Mehta (GTM) — attach this doc to intake ticket and loop engineering/finance.
- Quick Slack channel for listing coordination: #marketplace-onboarding

End of doc
